target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport, a 429 response with a server `Retry-After` header was turned into a plain `Error` with no status or cooldown attached, so no component in the retry path could honor the server's window. Auto-retry fell back to fixed exponential backoff and, with `maxRetries: 3`, all retries could land inside a still-active rate-limit window and fail the turn.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The bespoke Anthropic fetch client is not a Stainless-style SDK, so the parsed `Retry-After` was discarded before reaching any retry owner. Fixing this correctly requires the server cooldown to reach **every** retry owner — the in-turn `AgentSession.prepareRetry`, the embedded-runner failover, and the auth-profile cooldown — as **one consistent value**.

## The closed `ServerRetryAfter` representation

A server cooldown has three meaningful states, so it is modelled as a closed discriminated union (in `packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`) rather than a `number` that overloads `Infinity` as an over-limit sentinel:

```ts
export type ServerRetryAfter =
  | { kind: "seconds"; seconds: number } // finite server cooldown
  | { kind: "unbounded" };               // overflowed / unparseably-large header
// undefined = no usable Retry-After
```

An earlier `number`-with-`Infinity` shape let finite-only downstreams silently drop the over-limit case (this is exactly the defect the prior review cycles kept surfacing in different layers). The closed union makes every consumer handle `unbounded` explicitly — TypeScript exhaustiveness enforces it — so the over-limit signal can never be lost.

## Changes (threaded end to end)

- **Transport** (`anthropic-transport-stream.ts`): non-OK responses throw with `httpStatus` and a `ServerRetryAfter` built from the canonical `parseRetryAfterSeconds` (an overflowed header → `{ kind: "unbounded" }`).
- **Extraction** (`transport-stream-shared.ts`): the `ServerRetryAfter` union is carried onto the `AssistantMessage` as a validated closed object (no `Infinity` in a number field).
- **In-turn retry** (`llm/utils/retry.ts` `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs`): finite cooldown ≤ `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` is honored as a lower bound; a finite cooldown above it, or `unbounded`, returns `null` (stop in-turn retry → fallback). `maxRetryDelayMs` is now the **only** in-turn sleep ceiling.
- **Embedded failover** (`assistant-failover.ts`): `unbounded` (and finite > 60s) never triggers a same-model short-window retry; it routes to profile rotation and passes the union to the profile-failure mark.
- **Auth-profile cooldown** (`auth-profiles/usage.ts`): a finite cooldown extends the profile window; `unbounded` holds the profile for the maximum timer-safe window (`MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`) instead of collapsing to the ordinary first-failure backoff — closing the "profile eligible during an unknown provider cooldown" gap.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a `Retry-After` within the configured tolerance now delay retries by at least the server window (rate-limited turns wait it out and can succeed). Cooldowns beyond the tolerance — including malformed/overflowed headers — fail fast for fallback and hold the auth profile for the full unknown window, instead of retrying inside it.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (real managed transport + real resolver + real embedded routing).** A real Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header, driven through the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` (real `buildGuardedModelFetch`); the propagated closed union is fed into the real `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` (default `maxRetryDelayMs=60000`) and the real `isShortWindowRateLimitMessage` failover router:

```
== Path A: managed transport -> AssistantMessage.retryAfter -> resolveAutoRetryDelayMs (max=60000) ==
  retry-after: 30           -> retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":30}  delay=30000ms
  retry-after: 120          -> retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":120} delay=null (stop in-turn retry -> fallback)
  retry-after-ms overflow   -> retryAfter={"kind":"unbounded"}             delay=null (stop in-turn retry -> fallback)
== Path B: embedded failover routing (isShortWindowRateLimitMessage) ==
  {seconds:30}  -> sameModelShortRetry=true
  {seconds:120} -> sameModelShortRetry=false
  {unbounded}   -> sameModelShortRetry=false  (routes to profile rotation)
```

Before this fix (origin/main) the same 429 yields no status/cooldown and a fixed 2000ms backoff.

**Focused tests (cross-layer, incl. overflow → profile).**
- `retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts` — finite lower-bound, boundary at max, reject > max, reject `unbounded`, honor > 60s when the operator raises the max.
- `provider-transport-fetch.test.ts` — canonical parser incl. overflow → `Infinity`.
- `transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — the `unbounded` union survives extraction; resolver rejects it.
- `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — a 429 with an overflowed `retry-after-ms` surfaces `retryAfter={kind:"unbounded"}` through the real transport.
- `auth-profiles/usage.test.ts` — **an over-limit (unbounded) cooldown holds the profile for `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`** (the overflow-header-to-profile regression), and a finite cooldown extends the window.

```
$ npx vitest run <transport + retry + failover + auth-profile suites>
 Test Files  11 passed (11)
      Tests  723 passed (723)
```

Full source typechecks clean (`tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`); oxlint reports 0 warnings / 0 errors on all changed files.

---

## Exact-head real behavior proof (finite recovery + persisted profile cooldown)

**Finite Retry-After — turn recovers after the wait** (real managed transport; server 429+`Retry-After: 3` then 200 SSE; the real `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` delay is slept between attempts):

```
attempt#1: stopReason=error retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":3}
resolved wait=3000ms; slept 3007ms
attempt#2: stopReason=stop text="recovered"
server_requests=2  => turn recovered after the server-specified wait
```

**Over-limit — persisted auth-profile cooldown** (real `markAuthProfileFailure` against a real in-memory `AuthProfileStore`; profile id redacted to a sha256 by the subsystem logger):

```
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: profile=sha256:154a23a3efe6 provider=anthropic reason=rate_limit window=cooldown
retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":120} -> persisted cooldown ≈ now + 120000ms
retryAfter={"kind":"unbounded"}             -> persisted cooldown ≈ now + 2147000001ms (== MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS)
```

## Maintainer decisions requested

Two aspects are intentional and want maintainer sign-off (they are policy/contract choices, not defects):

1. **Shared contract:** `AssistantMessage` gains optional `httpStatus?` and `retryAfter?: ServerRetryAfter`. Additive and type-compatible; consumed by the Anthropic transport, `AgentSession` retry, embedded failover, and auth-profile cooldown.
2. **Unbounded cooldown policy:** an overflowed/unparseable provider `Retry-After` suppresses the affected auth profile for `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`. This is deliberately conservative (the real provider window is unknown, so the profile is not retried into it); happy to adjust the ceiling if a shorter bound is preferred.
